title: review: B1 v3: planner_runs routing integration — taxonomy → router → tier per headless decision, mode off byte-identical, shadow Opus launch, hold instead of downgrade, telemetry rows and skip rows, re-escalation (P3, P5, P6, P9, P15, P17)
spec:
Why: planner_runs.run_group/launch_routed (planner_runs.py:1090-1236) launch every escalate-route decision on [models].planner (Fable); tick() drops routine/none points silently; run_group's early returns (same state_version, goal launch active, already decided) leave no record; usage is logged only as bus.log_run planner_decision rows. The Wave A modules are merged on goal/T-0674: planner_taxonomy.classify(point, ctx, *, goal, task); planner_router.load_cfg / fable_reserve_ok / effective_complexity / hard_escalation / decide(classification, ctx, route, *, cfg, availability, evidence, jev_signal, sample) / record(decision, *, subject, route, jev_signal, root) / RouterDecision(tier, mode, hard, hold, hold_reason, reasons, hard_reasons, soft_score, shadow_tier, candidates, evidence, decision_type); planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage/snapshot/materiality/record_materiality/record_skip/read_invocations; jev_planner.should_ask(router_mode, jev_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route_name: str)/ask(classification, ctx, goal, *, cfg, router_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route: str, state_version, task, ...); planner_shadow.eligible/launch/parse/record/score; planner_scorecard.class_evidence (returns reescalation_rate None and noninferior None for under-sampled classes, without raising). Spec reviews of T-0732 and T-0738 folded in; the Planner waived a third spec review.
What (planner_runs.py, decision.py, goals.py; new tests in tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py; existing tests keep passing):
- Imports in planner_runs.py: `from . import planner_taxonomy, planner_router, planner_telemetry, planner_shadow, jev_planner` (module references only; planner_telemetry already imports planner_runs, so never `from .planner_telemetry import name`); planner_scorecard imported lazily inside _class_evidence with try/except ImportError.
- goals.launch_planner(repo_path, prompt, account_id, max_budget_usd, log_path, extra_env=None, model=None): model None keeps cfg["models"]["planner"]; argv otherwise unchanged. launch_routed(pool, route, prompt, account, budget, log) becomes a thin resolver: tier = route.tier or "fable"; model = models["planner"] if tier == "fable" else models.get(tier, tier); return goals.launch_planner(ROOT, prompt, account.id, budget, log, model=model). Delete the duplicated argv block (lines 1096-1109). Mode off therefore produces exactly the legacy argv.
- decision.route: kind "retrospective" -> routine "retrospective_deterministic"; ctx.get("state_unchanged") True -> none "unchanged_state" (checked right after the infra check). Existing tests unchanged.
- tick(): sections are 4-tuples (point, ctx, route, classification). Before routing each point: ctx["complexity"] = task complexity for held points else goal complexity; ctx["state_version"] = state_version(goal_id); ctx["state_unchanged"] = (_goal_launches().get(goal_id) or {}).get("last_state_version") == ctx["state_version"]; classification = planner_taxonomy.classify(point, ctx, goal=goal, task=task). Every point that does not reach run_group records planner_telemetry.record_skip(goal_id=..., event="tick", reason=..., kind=..., payload_key=...) with reason routine, none:<route reason>, fix_round_in_flight, or unknown_gate.
- run_group(sections, pool): every unpack site becomes 4-tuples (`for point, ctx, section_route, classification in sections`, the _blocked filter, the _claim loop, the record update loop, the skip loop, the running-record loop). Its early returns record skips for every section: same state_version -> record_skip(reason="same_state_version"), goal launch active -> "goal_launch_active", already decided -> "already_decided" (event "run_group"); the session-attached and no-headroom paths already call _record_skip and additionally call planner_telemetry.record_skip with reasons "planner_session_attached" / "no_account_headroom". Leader section = max over sections by (route priority investigate 1 / escalate 2, planner_router.effective_complexity(classification, ctx), then the smallest payload_key string); its route, ctx and classification drive the decision and the telemetry row. rcfg = planner_router.load_cfg(pool.cfg). availability = {rcfg["default_tier"]: {"available": models alias configured and account is not None, "reason": "ok" or why}, rcfg["escalation_tier"]: same, "fable_reserve_ok": planner_router.fable_reserve_ok(headroom_share, rcfg)} with headroom_share None when the picked account's daily_budget is 0 else 1 - (day_tokens + planner_day_tokens) / daily_budget. evidence = _class_evidence(model, classification, pool): calls planner_scorecard.class_evidence(models[default_tier], decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, root=STATE, cfg=pool.cfg) under try/except Exception; in BOTH the success and the failure path normalise to {"n": int(evidence.get("n") or 0), "noninferior": evidence.get("noninferior") (True/False/None), "reescalation_rate": float(evidence.get("reescalation_rate") or 0.0)} so soft_score never sees None. Re-escalation (P15): if the goal's latest invocation row (planner_telemetry.read_invocations() filtered by goal_id, max started_at) has tier == rcfg["default_tier"] and (decision_type == "architectural_replan" or ctx spec_review_request_changes >= rcfg["hard_spec_review_request_changes_min"] or the lineage cap is reached), set ctx["reescalation"] = True before hard_escalation. hard_reasons = planner_router.hard_escalation(classification, ctx, route, rcfg). jev_signal = jev_planner.ask(classification, ctx, goal, cfg=rcfg, router_mode=rcfg["mode"], hard_reasons=hard_reasons, availability=availability, route=route.name, state_version=ctx["state_version"], task=held task or None) only when jev_planner.should_ask(rcfg["mode"], rcfg["jev_mode"], hard_reasons, availability, route.name)[0]; route.name (the plain string) in BOTH calls, never the Route object. sample = random.random(); decision = planner_router.decide(classification, ctx, route, cfg=rcfg, availability=availability, evidence=evidence, jev_signal=jev_signal, sample=sample); planner_router.record(decision, subject=goal_id, route=route, jev_signal=jev_signal).
- Effects: decision.hold -> every section record gets status "held_for_fable", hold_reason = decision.hold_reason, notify.notify_once(goal_id, f"held_for_fable:{launch_id}", ...); return {"launched": False, "reason": decision.hold_reason}; the next tick retries (records in status held_for_fable never block and are never claimed). Otherwise before_snapshot = planner_telemetry.snapshot(goal_id); launched = launch_routed(pool, dataclasses.replace(route, tier=decision.tier), prompt, account, budget, log); planner_telemetry.record_launch(launch_id=launch_id, goal_id, event="tick", decision_type, kind=leader kind, payload_keys=[per section: the bare held task id (payload_key.split(':')[0]) when kind == held else payload_key], model=resolved model id, tier=decision.tier, account=account.id, complexity=ctx["complexity"], band, task_class, architectural, route=route.name, route_reason=route.reason, mode=rcfg["mode"], state_version=ctx["state_version"], packet_chars=len(prompt), started_at=now, reescalation=bool(ctx.get("reescalation"))); records store telemetry_before and launch_started_at. Shadow: ok, why = planner_shadow.eligible(decision, rcfg, sample=sample); when ok: account_dict = the [[claude_accounts]] entry whose id == account.id; shadow = planner_shadow.launch(prompt, model=models[decision.shadow_tier], account=account_dict, budget_usd=limits.max_budget_usd.planner_shadow default 1.5, log=STATE/runs/f"planner-shadow-{goal_id}-{launch_id}.log"); when shadow is not None store shadow_pid, shadow_pid_start=goals._proc_start(shadow["pid"]), shadow_log, shadow_started_at, shadow_tier on the records; exceptions printed to stderr and ignored.
- _record_decision_usage(r): additionally planner_telemetry.record_usage(r["launch_id"], input_tokens=..., output_tokens=..., cache_read_tokens=..., cache_write_tokens=..., usd=..., latency_s=now - r["launch_started_at"], outcome=..., session_id=...) when the record has launch_id.
- reconcile(): when a running record's process is gone and telemetry_before exists: planner_telemetry.record_materiality(launch_id, before, planner_telemetry.snapshot(goal_id)) once (flag materiality_logged). When shadow_log exists and not goals.identity_of(shadow_pid, shadow_pid_start): parsed = planner_shadow.parse(shadow_log); row = planner_shadow.record(launch_id=..., goal_id, decision_type, state_version, model, tier=shadow_tier, started_at=shadow_started_at, parsed, latency_s); r["shadow_agreement"] = planner_shadow.score(row, materiality) once (flag shadow_logged).
Tests use the sandbox pattern of tests/test_planner_runs.py; patch goals.Popen / planner_shadow popen, and for the Jev case patch jev.ask (the network function) rather than jev_planner.ask so the real should_ask/ask string contract is exercised.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_mode_off_argv_identical_to_legacy — with [planner.routing].mode off, run_group produces exactly the argv that goals.launch_planner produced before this change for the same decision (captured via patched Popen, compared list-equal), one Popen call only, and no held_for_fable record

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_shadow_mode_launches_fable_then_opus_shadow_without_bus_writes — shadow mode: the first Popen argv uses models.planner and .mcp.planner.json, the second uses models.opus, .mcp.planner-shadow.json and --disallowedTools; bus task files and plan.md are byte-identical after the shadow launch; the record carries shadow_log and shadow_pid_start; a launch row exists with tier fable, mode shadow and packet_chars

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_hard_decision_holds_when_fable_unavailable — active mode, goal complexity 9, escalation tier unavailable: no Popen call, every section record has status held_for_fable with hold_reason starting fable_unavailable, one notify_once, and a second tick with the tier available launches instead of giving up

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_skips_usage_materiality_and_jev_invocation — a routine point, an unchanged-state goal and a run_group same_state_version early return each produce planner_skips rows with reasons routine, none:unchanged_state and same_state_version; on a shadow-mode escalate decision with two available tiers and no hard reasons, a patched jev.ask is called exactly once and the planner_jev row has asked True (so should_ask/ask received the route name string), while a hard decision never calls jev.ask; an under-sampled class_evidence result (reescalation_rate None) does not raise; a launched decision followed by a fake exit whose log carries usage yields usage and materiality rows under the same launch_id, materiality naming the task created during the run

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_reescalation_forces_fable_after_opus_and_tie_break — a goal whose latest invocation row has tier opus and whose held point has spec_review_request_changes 2 launches on models.planner in active mode with reescalation True in the launch row and a planner_route decision row whose hard_constraints contain repeated_spec_rejection and reescalation; two escalate sections in one group pick the leader with the higher effective complexity, then the smaller payload_key; tests/test_decision.py::test_retrospective_and_unchanged_state_routes — kind retrospective routes routine retrospective_deterministic and state_unchanged True routes none unchanged_state

result.summary: Diff matches the spec closely: imports, launch_routed/goals.launch_planner model threading, decision.route ordering, tick()'s per-point telemetry skips, run_group's leader selection/availability/evidence/reescalation/hard-escalation/jev/shadow wiring, and reconcile's materiality+shadow scoring all line up with the packet and are covered by the new tests. Two non-blocking issues found: a telemetry-reason race in the session-attached/no-headroom skip path (re-derives _session_attached() instead of reusing it, can produce inconsistent skip reasons), and a broader-than-specified except clause in _class_evidence that could silently mask evidence-pipeline bugs. Neither breaks the stated acceptance criteria.

comments.issue: run_group's no-account/session-attached skip path calls _session_attached() a second time to pick the planner_telemetry.record_skip reason, instead of reusing the boolean already computed a few lines above for _record_skip's reason. If session attachment state changes between the two calls (e.g. during pool.pick()), the bus-level skip reason and the telemetry skip reason for the same event can disagree ("no account with headroom" vs "planner_session_attached"), corrupting the telemetry this spec is meant to make trustworthy.

_class_evidence wraps planner_scorecard.class_evidence in `except Exception: pass`, where the spec calls for `except ImportError`. Any non-import error (corrupted scorecard state, cfg shape mismatch, future signature drift) is silently swallowed and evidence falls back to n=0/noninferior=None, masking real bugs in the evidence pipeline instead of surfacing them.
